描述_EN: grass slippers (cao xie) are among the oldest and simplest forms of outdoor footwear in china, with soles made from woven rice straw and uppers of plaited rush. traditionally, family members of the deceased would wear undyed coarse hemp clothing and headbands, along with straw sandals, at a funeral to express filial piety, putting aside personal appearance and comfort to grieve for the passing of loved ones. peasants wore straw shoes such as these while working in the fields, gathering firewood and herbs, or hunting in the mountains, regardless of the weather. although the shoes look uncomfortable to wear, their coarse soles grip efficiently to slippery surfaces. by displaying useful and commercial goods from across the world made from discarded materials, the museum aimed to promote corporate awareness of environmental sustainability and drive innovative uses from scraps or surplus materials. sandals made from straw were even fitted to the hooves of cattle and pigs to wear while being led along muddy roads. in china, straw shoes are also associated with mourning. these close-toe slippers were originally acquired for the v&a’s bethnal green branch, which opened in 1872, to illustrate the use of waste products.
描述_ZN: 草鞋是中国最古老和最简单的户外鞋类形式之一，鞋底由稻草编织而成，鞋面由草编而成。 传统上，死者的家人会在葬礼上穿上未染色的粗麻衣和头巾，再加上草鞋，以表达孝心，抛开个人的外表和舒适感，为亲人的离去而悲伤。 农民穿着这样的草鞋在田间劳作，收集柴火和草药，或在山上打猎，无论天气如何。 虽然这种鞋看起来不舒服，但它们的粗鞋底能有效地抓紧湿滑的表面。 通过展示来自世界各地的由废弃材料制成的有用和商业商品，该博物馆旨在促进企业对环境可持续性的认识，并推动对废品或剩余材料的创新利用。 用稻草做的鞋甚至被装在牛和猪的蹄子上，以便在泥泞的道路上被牵着走。 在中国，草鞋也与丧事有关。 这些贴脚拖鞋最初是为1872年开业的V&a's bethnal green分店购买的，以说明废品的使用情况。
